def tuple_str_int(s):
    """Converts a string representation of a tuple to an actual integer tuple."""
    return eval(f"({s})")  # Wrap in parentheses if not already present, though input usually is fine. 
                          # A safer alternative without eval (see below).

# Safer approach using split and map:
def safe_tuple_str_int(s):
    """Converts a string like '(7, 8)' to tuple(7, 8) safely."""
    if not s.startswith('(') or not s.endswith(')'):
        raise ValueError("String must be enclosed in parentheses")
    
    # Remove the outer parentheses and split by comma
    content = s[1:-1] 
    parts = [int(x.strip()) for x in content.split(',')]
    return tuple(parts)

# Test cases
assert safe_tuple_str_int("(7, 8, 9)") == (7, 8, 9)
print("All tests passed.")
